details: CONFIRMED by reading. Q1's verdict rests on its failing-case test (judge Check mode: "Run the tests the fixer named for
each finding"; "Q1 is MET only when its failing-case test also fails without the fix"). The only fixer of Q1 in a
change-kind unit is the build worker, whose report is S/reports/<name>.md (the build prompt, line 191). fixesText at
line 216 starts from `fixes` ('none' or fix-x.md) and the fixgate reports; the worker report is never added. The old
split had one reason the design (3.3) says was not recorded: the queue check was given the worker's report, the
whole check the review fixer's. Merging the two checkers without merging their Fixes lines leaves the checker to hunt
for Q1's test or answer q1_test empty, which stops the unit at check (line 170). Outcome on a real run is PLAUSIBLE
(an agent may find the test by itself); the missing input is confirmed. No test asserts the check prompt's Fixes.
Size: 10 agent minutes.
evidence: cycle.js:206-216 fixes = 'none' | fix-x.md; finish(... fixes: fixesText(fixes, st) ...)
failing_case: args {base: "master", relay: true, scratch: S, items: [{name: "x", wt, check, branch: "wt/x", item: "the-item"}]},
review answers inside 0. The check prompt reads "Check: `S/reports/review-x.json`. Fixes: `none`. ..." and must return
q1_test for Q1. The worker's report S/reports/x.md, which names the failing-case test for the queue item, is in no
prompt the checker sees. Today's script gave the queue check `Fixes: S/reports/x.md` (relay-change-cycle line 72).
With review inside 1 the check gets `Fixes: S/reports/fix-x.md` only: again not the worker's report.
Should be: the check of a change (kind change) names the worker's report among its fixes.
fix_hint: In changeUnit, for kind change (not built) start the fixes list with `${S}/reports/${it.name}.md`, then the review
fix report, then the fixgate reports; add a test on the "check: x" prompt for cases 1-3.
pass_cases: 1. kind change, item "the-item", review inside 0: the "check: x" prompt contains "S/reports/x.md" in its Fixes.
2. kind change, review inside 1: Fixes names both S/reports/x.md and S/reports/fix-x.md.
3. kind change, red gate before review then green: Fixes names S/reports/x.md and S/reports/fixgate-x-1.md.
4. kind fix: Fixes is the front's `fixes` (plus any fixgate report), unchanged from today.
5. kind recheck with no items and no red gate: Fixes stays `none`.
findings.summary: the one checker of a change never gets the build worker's report, so Q1 (the queue item, which the worker fixed) has no fixer report naming its test

details: CONFIRMED by reading (outcome PLAUSIBLE: needs a dead runner). The design (3.4, retry_dead) calls a retry safe because
"a second gate on the same worktree waits on relay-gate.lock and reuses the log" — true only for relay mode. In project
mode the gate is the project's raw command; nothing locks it, and the prompt (line 116) is the same text on the retry
(ask() line 89-101 resends the prompt unchanged). The runner is told to run detached, so the first gate outlives its
runner. Gate runners died in about 10 of 151 units (design, r2's count), so the case is reachable whenever project mode
is used. Size: 15 agent minutes.
evidence: cycle.js:89-101 ask(): for t in 0..retry_dead: agent(prompt, opts) with the same prompt
cycle.js:110 const log = `${S}/gate-${it.name}-${n}.log` (n is the same on the retry)
cycle.js:116 project prompt: `{ ...; ${A.gate}; echo "exit $?"; } > ${log} 2>&1`, run detached
design r3 3.4: "safe: a second gate on the same worktree waits on relay-gate.lock and reuses the log"
failing_case: relay false, gate "make test", retry_dead 1 (default). gate 1 runner starts
`{ echo head ...; make test; echo "exit $?"; } > S/gate-x-1.log 2>&1` detached, then dies without StructuredOutput.
ask() retries under the same label with the same prompt: the new runner starts a second `make test` in the same
worktree writing `> S/gate-x-1.log` (truncating the file the first one still writes into). Two gates run at once on one
worktree, and the log holds both runs' lines; its head/exit lines may come from different runs, which the checker's
Gate rule then reads as the gate of the head.
Should be: the retry waits on the gate already running (or a fresh log per attempt with no second gate started).
fix_hint: Have the project gate prompt write the pid to `${log}.pid` and say: if that pid is alive, wait on it and report its log
instead of starting the gate. Or skip the retry for the project gate (stop at gate with the error).
pass_cases: 1. project mode, gate 1 throws once then answers: the retry prompt tells the runner to look for a live gate started
for this log (for example a pid file next to it) and wait on it rather than start one.
2. project mode, first gate runner answers: one gate prompt, as today.
3. relay mode retry: unchanged (relay gate waits on relay-gate.lock and reuses the log; the design measured it).
reason: tests/test_cycle_workflow.py:371 passes, fails without fix (prompt-level guard)
findings.summary: project mode: a retried gate runner starts a second detached gate over the same log while the dead runner's gate still runs

details: CONFIRMED by reading. Names depend only on unit name and the per-run counter (newState starts at 0 each run). The
check record itself is safe (the check-mark hook commits it into .relay/checks), so the loss is a scratch fixer report
and, in project mode, an earlier gate log. Size: 10 agent minutes.
evidence: cycle.js:140 newState() { gn: 0, fn: 0 } per unit run; cycle.js:110, 132, 164 names from it.name and the counters
failing_case: Change run for x: gate 1 red, fix red gate 1 writes S/reports/fixgate-x-1.md; check open 1. The front runs kind fix
with fixes "S/reports/fix-x.md and S/reports/fixgate-x-1.md". Its gate 1 is red: fix red gate 1 writes
S/reports/fixgate-x-1.md again, overwriting the first report, and the check's Fixes reads
"... fixgate-x-1.md and fixgate-x-1.md". Today's scripts used distinct names (fixgate-/fixgate3- in the change cycle,
fixgate2- and gate-x-f<n>.log in the fix cycle).
fix_hint: Put the kind in the names (e.g. `fixgate-${kind}-${name}-${n}`, `gate-${kind}-${name}-${n}.log`), or a run tag arg.
pass_cases: 1. kind fix after a change run with a red gate: no report path the change run wrote is written again.
2. kind change: report names as today (fixgate-x-1.md, gate-x-1.log).
findings.summary: a fix-kind run reuses the change run's report names (fixgate-x-1.md, gate-x-1.log, check-x.json), overwriting the earlier fixer report the front passes in `fixes`

details: CONFIRMED by reading; the design (9, step 1) says "the script runs steps 3-7". Size: 5 agent minutes.
evidence: SKILL.md:102 "runs steps 2-7 for each change in a run"; SKILL.md step 2 "Before it, the reproduce step ... before relay queue take"
failing_case: A front reads "The script ... runs steps 2-7" for a fix item whose failing_kind is claim, and starts the run without the
reproduce step; the script builds at once (the 24 Oct bench case cost about 34 minutes and 123k tokens). Also the
paragraph names args but no unit fields: a relay-mode unit without `branch`, or a fix unit without `findings`, is learnt
only from the refusal line.
fix_hint: Reword to "runs the build of step 2 and steps 3-7 (the reproduce step comes before the run)" and add one line of unit fields.
pass_cases: 1. The paragraph says the script runs the build of step 2 and steps 3-7, and the reproduce step stays before the run.
2. The paragraph names the unit fields: name, wt, check, branch (relay mode), item; fix: fix, fixes, findings; recheck:
reason: SKILL.md lines 102-115 now state the reproduce step is before the run and name the unit fields
findings.summary: the skill says the script runs steps 2-7, but step 2's reproduce step (claim items, before the take) is not in the script, and the unit fields the script requires are not named
